All four edges carry numeric weight and begin unresolved under the extended reading. Consequently the environment does not solve the graph for the agent. No waiting is required by these effect contracts. ## findings

### T1-1 — SOURCE-POLICY RED and SOURCE-TASK RED: incompatible request lifecycle

Shared root cause and exact conflicting quotations are in [_difficulty.md / P1](env/enterprise_cloud_service_accounting/audits/policy_task/storage_accounting/_difficulty.md#findings). Task-specific demonstration is in the frozen policy_self_consistency section: base-compliant pending claim contributes0 while posted tool claim contributes215; occurrence September12 required versus September5 retained. Gold step6 and step12 use precisely these contradictory effects. The solvability proof quotes the full base pending/current-time sentence as satisfied=true at both steps despite contrary tool effect. Thus its asserted base compliance is false. Affected task fields: evaluation_criteria[6], evaluation_criteria[12], their solvability gold_actions base_preconditions, and the resulting Q/A status/occurred_at. First audit; no preceding revision.

### T1-2 — SOURCE-TASK RED: authorization argument is not uniquely entailed

Symptom: pre-reveal derivation selected original payment P for authorize_storage_refund.storage_event_id; gold selects incident I. Root cause: the contract permits a generic evidence reference, the function ignores storage_event_id entirely, and the source policy supplies no applicable requirement choosing the incident for a refund authorization.

Verbatim tool arg at task_tools.py lines114–116: “storage_event_id: Id class — Identifier of the selected storage evidence or assessment copied from find_storage_events, find_storage_holdings, find_customers or the corresponding completed action receipt.” The body updates request_id with source_event_id, related_event_id, holding, amount, status and notice; it never reads storage_event_id. Original payment P and incident I are both reachable storage evidence in find_storage_events. The original-payment destination and exact authorization amount are already bound separately to P, A, K and235.

Concrete alternatives at the same handling moment, with all other arguments identical:

- Gold: storage_event_id=83a2ebe5-6666-47f9-9c42-69384a87d2b5 (incident).
- Independent: storage_event_id=8a89f81c-a582-47d2-a565-af8700533956 (original payment).

Both calls produce exactly the same posted authorization235, same original payment/source and concession link, same state and receipt “Recorded 89e76b3c-1312-4bbc-a5da-d3368beb4549: USD 235.00.” This was confirmed by executing the actual function body against in-memory copies, with evidence in [authorization_argument_counterexample.json](env/enterprise_cloud_service_accounting/audits/policy_task/storage_accounting/authorization_argument_counterexample.json). This is not an arbitrary accepted negative case: each candidate satisfies the broad affirmative argument description and the actual refund business object requirement. The incident is only selected in GT's hidden claim_deadline binding, which is explicitly conditional on service_credit request subtype and does not apply to this refund form. GT's choice is therefore not unique under source policy. Affected evaluation_criteria[12].arguments.arguments.storage_event_id and argument_uniqueness_tracing, solvability gold action step12, task tool contract. First audit; no previous revision. No artifact fix is prescribed.

Final verdicts: SOURCE-POLICY RED (T1-1); numeric dependency edges individually load-bearing and unresolved under extended reading, but merged policy cannot resolve filing consistently; SOURCE-TASK RED (T1-1 and T1-2). Overall task1 RED.
